title: Absolute affine-square embedding of a monic relative relation
statement: Let $S,U,R$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], with morphisms $U\to S$ and $R\to S$. Suppose a commutative ring $A$ and an isomorphism $U\cong\operatorname{Spec}A$ are given [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Put $V=U\times_SU$ and $P=U\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}U$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $k:V\to P$ be the canonical morphism whose two projections to $U$ are those of $V$. Let $j:R\to V$ be an $S$-morphism which is a monomorphism, meaning that $j\circ a=j\circ b$ implies $a=b$ for every scheme $T$ and morphisms $a,b:T\to R$. Then $P\cong\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_{\mathbf Z}A)$ compatibly with the two projections. Both $k$ and $q=k\circ j$ are monomorphisms, $q:R\to P$ is separated [def-weil-proper-morphism], and the absolute structure morphism $R\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is separated. No finite-type condition on $j$ and no separatedness condition on $S$ are required.

source.place: Tag 0265, lemma-presentation-quasi-compact, first proof paragraph: monomorphism of the relative square into the absolute affine square and separatedness of R.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] with base ring $\mathbf Z$ and both algebras $A$. The given isomorphism $U\cong\operatorname{Spec}A$ induces an isomorphism on the two-factor fibre products by their universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]. Thus $P\cong\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_{\mathbf Z}A)$, with the two projections given by $a\mapsto a\otimes1$ and $a\mapsto1\otimes a$. In particular $P$ is affine.

source.place: Tag 01I4, lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes; Stacks 0265 opening proof paragraph, absolute affine square.

proof.text: Write $p_1,p_2:V\to U$ and $r_1,r_2:P\to U$ for the projections. The definition [def-pc-fibre-product] gives $r_i\circ k=p_i$. For any scheme $T$ and $a,b:T\to V$ with $k\circ a=k\circ b$, composing with $r_i$ gives $p_i\circ a=p_i\circ b$ for both $i$. Uniqueness in the universal property of $V$ gives $a=b$. Hence $k$ is monic. For $a,b:T\to R$, the equation $q\circ a=q\circ b$ first cancels $k$ and then cancels the given monomorphism $j$, so $a=b$. Hence $q$ is monic.

source.place: Tag 0265, lemma-presentation-quasi-compact, first proof paragraph: the monomorphism into U times U, expanded by the fibre-product universal property.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-scheme-monomorphism-separated] to the monomorphism $q:R\to P$ proved in step 2. It gives precisely that $q$ is separated, without a finite-type hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 01L4, lemma-monomorphism-separated; applied in the opening paragraph of Spaces Tag 0265.

proof.text: The morphism $q:R\to P$ is separated by step 3 and its target $P$ is affine by step 1. Therefore [lem-sc-separated-over-affine-scheme-separated] applied to $q$ says that $R\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is separated. These are all conclusions. The comparison argument used only the fibre-product universal property, and the separatedness result used only monicity and the affine target; neither finite type of $j$ nor separatedness of $S$ was used.

lean.statement: theorem affine_square_monomorphism_absolute_separated (S U R : Scheme.{u}) (f : U ⟶ S) (r : R ⟶ S) (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (e : U ≅ Spec (CommRingCat.of A)) (j : R ⟶ pullback f f) (hj : j ≫ pullback.fst f f ≫ f = r) [Mono j] : (∃ eP : pullback (terminal.from U) (terminal.from U) ≅ Spec (CommRingCat.of (A ⊗[ℤ] A)), eP.hom ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeftRingHom : A →+* A ⊗[ℤ] A)) = pullback.fst (terminal.from U) (terminal.from U) ≫ e.hom ∧ eP.hom ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight : A →ₐ[ℤ] A ⊗[ℤ] A).toRingHom) = pullback.snd (terminal.from U) (terminal.from U) ≫ e.hom) ∧ Mono (Scheme.relativeToAbsoluteSquare f) ∧ Mono (j ≫ Scheme.relativeToAbsoluteSquare f) ∧ IsSeparated (j ≫ Scheme.relativeToAbsoluteSquare f) ∧ IsSeparated (terminal.from R)
